mainTopic: Having sons through conduct and תפילה; why בית שמאי treat all who die as נדות and זבין; the impurity of blood from a woman after death, and דם תבוסה
overview: The amud opens at the end of רבי יהושע's advice on how to have sons. The advice is to marry a fitting wife and act with holiness during תשמיש. When the questioners say this often does not work, he adds that one must pray to הקב״ה, to Whom children belong. The גמרא concludes that both are needed. רבי חמא ברבי חנינא then explains 'שכר פרי הבטן' as a reward for a husband who puts his wife first. Next, the גמרא asks why בית שמאי say every woman who dies is a נדה. It rejects the idea that fear of the מלאך המות brings on blood. It concludes instead that this is a תקנה to protect the dignity of living נדות, and likewise of living זבין. A new משנה then discusses blood that comes out of a woman after death, with disputes about כתם impurity and אהל impurity. The גמרא explains these disputes through the impurity of the מקור and through דם תבוסה, which a ברייתא then defines. The ברייתא's final case, blood dripping into a hole, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Sanctify yourself at the time of intimacy
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי יהושע's first answer: to have sons, a man should conduct himself with holiness during תשמיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he should sanctify himself at the time of intimacy.
steps.whatsHappening: We are coming in at the end of רבי יהושע's answer to the question 'What should a person do to have sons?' The full answer is: marry a fitting wife, and conduct yourself in holiness at the time of תשמיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the answer, marrying a suitable wife, comes just before this line. This line adds the second half, which is about personal conduct: modesty and holiness during intimacy. The next step will challenge this whole answer.

keyTerms.meaning: He should sanctify himself, meaning he should act with holiness and modesty

phrases.english: and he should sanctify himself
at the time of intimacy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יהושע's answer, which began before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To have sons, marry a fitting wife and act with holiness during תשמיש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proper, holy conduct during intimacy is one path to having sons.

steps.title: Many tried this and it did not work
steps.stepSummary: The people of אלכסנדריא object: many people followed this advice and still did not have sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Many people did this, and it did not help them!
steps.whatsHappening: The questioners push back against רבי יהושע's answer. They point out that real life shows this advice does not always work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge comes from experience. If proper conduct guaranteed sons, everyone who followed it would have sons, but many did not. So the advice cannot be the full answer.

keyTerms.meaning: And it did not help them

phrases.english: They said: Many have done so,
and it did not help!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: הַרְבֵּה עָשׂוּ כֵּן, וְלֹא הוֹעִילוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the advice given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's claim that a fitting wife and holy conduct lead to sons.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Experience shows many people did exactly this and still had no sons, so it cannot be the deciding factor.

steps.title: Pray to the One to Whom children belong
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers that one must pray to הקב״ה, because children are a gift from Him, as the פסוק in תהלים says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he should ask for mercy from the One to Whom children belong, as it says: 'Behold, children are a heritage of ה׳; the fruit of the womb is a reward.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע responds to the challenge. He says the real key is תפילה, asking הקב״ה for children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals a shift: conduct alone is not the deciding factor. Children belong to הקב״ה, so one must ask Him for them. The פסוק calls children ה׳'s 'inheritance' to give, which proves that they come from Him.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which introduces a different or corrected answer
He should ask for mercy, meaning he should pray
A heritage or inheritance from ה׳
Fruit of the womb, meaning children

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a basic principle: human effort matters, but children ultimately come from הקב״ה through תפילה.

phrases.english: Rather, he should ask for mercy
from the One to Whom children belong,
as it is said: 'Behold, children are a heritage of ה׳;
the fruit of the womb is a reward.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא יְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים מִמִּי שֶׁהַבָּנִים שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirects to a higher cause: success depends on תפילה, not only on conduct.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Proper conduct by itself is what brings sons.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sons come from הקב״ה, so one must pray to Him.

steps.title: Then why give the first advice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if תפילה is the key, what was רבי יהושע teaching with his first advice about a fitting wife and holy conduct?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks a question about רבי יהושע's words. If the answer is really תפילה, why did he first tell them about marrying well and acting in holiness?
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems the final answer, תפילה, replaces the first answer, which would make the first answer pointless. The גמרא wants to know what the first answer adds. The next step answers.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
phrases.notes: He means: if תפילה is what really works, why did רבי יהושע first give the advice about the wife and holy conduct?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how step 3's answer fits with step 1's advice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the first advice adds if תפילה is the real key.

steps.title: One without the other is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: תפילה without proper conduct does not suffice. Both are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: That this without that does not suffice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. רבי יהושע was teaching that you need both: תפילה and the proper conduct together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second answer does not cancel the first one. It completes it. Proper conduct alone did not help, and step 5 adds that תפילה alone also is not enough.
steps.whatToRemember: To have sons, a person needs both proper conduct (a fitting wife and holiness) and תפילה. Neither one is enough alone.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהושע took back his first answer. The גמרא says both parts are required together.

phrases.english: That this without that
phrases.notes: 'This' is the תפילה, and 'that' is marrying a fitting wife and acting in holiness.

phrases.english: does not suffice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first advice is still needed, because תפילה alone does not suffice.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Proper conduct and תפילה are both required.

steps.title: What does 'the fruit of the womb is a reward' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the words 'שכר פרי הבטן' in the פסוק mean: a reward for what?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'the fruit of the womb is a reward'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the פסוק that רבי יהושע quoted and asks about its wording. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'reward' (שכר) usually comes for doing something. So the גמרא asks what action earns the reward of children.

phrases.english: What is 'the fruit of the womb is a reward'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the פסוק quoted in step 3 to explain its wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What act the פסוק is rewarding with children.

steps.title: The reward for a husband who puts his wife first
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא explains: a husband who holds back so that his wife reaches completion first is rewarded by הקב״ה with children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא says: As a reward for men who hold themselves back so that their wives emit seed first, הקב״ה gives him the reward of the fruit of the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא answers the question of step 6. The reward in the פסוק is for a husband who is considerate of his wife during intimacy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'reward' in the פסוק is explained as payment for a specific good act: the husband putting his wife first. This fits the earlier idea of holy conduct in step 1. Proper behavior during intimacy brings the blessing of children.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold themselves back or wait
The Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.whatToRemember: 'שכר פרי הבטן' means children are a reward for a husband who is considerate and puts his wife first.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina says:
As a reward for holding themselves back in the belly,
so that their wives emit seed first —
phrases.notes: The words in round brackets are in the usual printed גמרא but get left out; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, gives him
the reward of the fruit of the womb.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: בִּשְׂכַר שֶׁמְּשַׁהִין עַצְמָן בַּבֶּטֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The reward is for a husband who holds back so that his wife reaches completion first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Children are הקב״ה's reward for a husband who is considerate of his wife during intimacy.

steps.title: What is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling of בית שמאי and asks for its reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'בית שמאי say, etc.' What is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה, where בית שמאי say all women who die are treated as נדות, and asks what their reason is. This sets up the next few steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeing blood is what normally makes a woman a נדה, so it is surprising to give every dead woman that status. The גמרא wants to know what makes בית שמאי assume this.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who has seen menstrual blood and is טמא

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: בית שמאי say every woman who dies has the status of a נדה.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Beit Shammai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The גמרא goes back to the משנה after the earlier discussion about having children.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason behind בית שמאי's rule that all women who die are נדות.

steps.title: First suggestion: fear of the Angel of Death brings blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a dying woman becomes so frightened that she sees blood, just as אסתר did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe it is because it is written 'and the queen was very distressed', and רב said this teaches that she became a נדה. Here too, because of her fright of the מלאך המות, a dying woman sees blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible reason, using the words 'אי נימא' ('if we say'). This is a suggestion that is about to be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב read the word וַתִּתְחַלְחַל as showing that אסתר's sudden fear made her see blood. The גמרא applies the same idea to a dying woman: the terror of the מלאך המות would make her see blood, so she dies a נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: And she was very distressed (אסתר). רב reads it as her body opening up from fear.
She began to see menstrual blood

steps.confusionAlert: 'אי נימא' means 'if you will say'. It signals a suggestion the גמרא will test and may later reject. It is not the final answer.

phrases.english: If we say it is because it is written:
"And the queen was greatly distressed"
and Rav said: This teaches that she began to menstruate.
Here too,
because of the fright of the Angel of Death,
she sees blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first possible answer to the question in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Fear of the מלאך המות causes a dying woman to see blood, as fear did to אסתר.

steps.title: But fear stops blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggestion with a משנה that says fear makes blood stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה that fear holds back the blood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the fear suggestion. An earlier משנה taught that fear prevents blood from coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If fear stops blood, then the fear of the מלאך המות should prevent blood, not cause it. The suggestion seems to say the opposite of a משנה.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a mishna
that fear holds back the blood!
phrases.notes: This refers to an earlier משנה in this מסכת (39a).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאֲנַן תְּנַן שֶׁחֲרָדָה מְסַלֶּקֶת אֶת הַדָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the fear reason given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that fright of the מלאך המות makes a woman see blood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה says fear stops blood. So fear cannot be what brings it on.

steps.title: Two kinds of fear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ongoing worry tightens the body, while sudden fright loosens it.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not difficult. Ongoing anxiety tightens the body and stops the blood. Sudden fright loosens it and brings blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by telling apart two kinds of fear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה about fear stopping blood is talking about פחדא, a long-lasting worry that tightens the body. The fright of the מלאך המות is ביעתותא, a sudden terror that loosens the body. So the fear reason still stands for now.

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
ongoing anxiety tightens,
phrases.notes: The body tightens up, so the blood is held in.

phrases.english: sudden fright loosens.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between two kinds of fear
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All fear stops blood, so fear could not cause a dying woman to see blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only ongoing anxiety stops blood. Sudden terror, like the fright of the מלאך המות, causes blood to flow.

steps.title: The men's case shows fear cannot be the reason
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי also say every man who dies is a זב, but a discharge caused by fear cannot make a man a זב. So fear cannot be their reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the ruling we learned: בית שמאי say all men die as זבים, and בית הלל say only a man who died as a זב is a זב? The Torah says 'from his flesh', meaning a discharge that comes on its own, and not one caused by an outside force!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel ruling of בית שמאי about men and uses it to knock down the fear reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If fear explained the women's case, it would also have to explain the men's case. But the Torah's word 'מבשרו' teaches that a זב discharge caused by an outside force, like fear, does not make a man טמא. So fear cannot explain בית שמאי's ruling about men, and the fear reason falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who becomes טמא through a certain kind of bodily discharge
From his flesh: the discharge must come from his own body on its own
Outside force, something beyond his control

steps.confusionAlert: The men's ruling is not a new question by itself. Its point is that the fear reason cannot work for men, so it cannot be בית שמאי's reason for women either.

phrases.english: But what about that which we learned:
Beit Shammai say:
all men die as zavim,
and Beit Hillel say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין זָב אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁמֵּת זָב.
phrases.english: only one who died as a zav is a zav.
I will apply here "from his flesh",
and not because of an outside force!
phrases.notes: Fear of the מלאך המות counts as an outside force, so it could not make a man a זב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new and stronger challenge to the fear reason, which survived step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fear reason for בית שמאי's ruling (step 9).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית שמאי rule the same way about men. But a discharge caused by fear is an outside force, and that cannot make a man a זב. So fear cannot be their reason.

steps.title: The real reason: protecting the honor of living נדות
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי's rule comes from a תקנה: vessels used by every dying woman are immersed, so that living נדות will not be embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the reason of בית שמאי is as a ברייתא teaches: at first, people would immerse vessels used by women who died as נדות, and living נדות were embarrassed. So they made a rule to immerse vessels used by all women, out of respect for living נדות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the fear reason and gives a new one: a rabbinic enactment based on honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Originally only the vessels of women who died as נדות were immersed. Living נדות were embarrassed, since this showed that their state stays with them even after death. To spare their feelings, the חכמים made the same practice apply to every woman who dies. That is why בית שמאי say all women die as נדות. The reason is a תקנה, not anything that physically happens to the body.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי's rule that all women die as נדות is not about fear or about blood. It is a תקנה to protect the dignity of living נדות, so that no woman is singled out.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the חכמים would broaden a ritual practice just to protect people from embarrassment.

phrases.english: Rather, the reason of Beit Shammai is as it is taught in a baraita:
At first they would immerse vessels
used by women who died as niddot,
and the living niddot were embarrassed.
So they enacted that they should immerse vessels
used by all women who die,
out of respect for the living niddot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the fear reason, which was rejected in step 12, with a new reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי's rule comes from a תקנה to immerse the vessels of every dying woman, out of respect for living נדות.

steps.title: The same enactment for dying men
steps.stepSummary: The source continues: at first, vessels used by dead זבין were immersed. This embarrassed living זבין, so the חכמים required immersion for the vessels of all dying men.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they would immerse the vessels used by זבין who died, and the living זבין were embarrassed. So they made a rule to immerse the vessels of all men, to protect the honor of living זבין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the source it began quoting in step 13. It now shows that the same kind of enactment was made for men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains the second half of בית שמאי's rule, that every man who dies is treated as a זב. It is not because fear caused a discharge, which was rejected in step 12. It is an enactment meant to protect living זבין from embarrassment.

keyTerms.meaning: Men who are impure because of a special bodily discharge (plural of זָב)

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי's rule that every dying man is a זב and every dying woman is a נדה comes from an enactment to protect living people from embarrassment. It is not a claim about what actually happens to the body at death.
steps.whyThisMatters: It finishes the answer to the challenge in step 12 by giving one reason that covers both the men and the women.

phrases.english: At first they would immerse
[the vessels] on account of זבין who died,
and the living זבין were embarrassed
so they enacted that they should immerse
on account of all the men,
because of the honor of the living זבין.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מַטְבִּילִין עַל גַּבֵּי זָבִין מֵתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same source quoted in step 13, applying it to men.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule for dying men is also an enactment, made to protect the dignity of living זבין.

steps.title: New משנה: blood that comes out of a woman after death
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. When a woman dies and a רביעית of blood comes out of her, the blood is impure as a כתם, and it is also impure in an אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman died, and a רביעית of blood came out of her. The blood makes things impure as a כתם, and it also makes things impure in an אהל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with the view of the תנא קמא about blood that comes out of a woman after she dies. He gives this blood two kinds of impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first impurity is that of a כתם, meaning the blood of a נדה. The second is impurity in an אהל, which applies to a רביעית of a dead person's blood. That is why the משנה mentions the amount of a רביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter-לוג, the amount of a dead person's blood that makes things impure
A blood stain, treated with the impurity of a נדה's blood
Tent or roof; impurity that spreads to everything under the same roof as a dead body

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate kinds of impurity here. כתם is impurity of a נדה's blood. אהל is impurity of a dead person. Keep them apart, because the rest of the משנה argues about each one separately.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A woman who died,
and a רביעית of blood came out of her
it makes things impure as a כתם,
and it makes things impure in an אהל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a related topic: blood that comes out of a woman at death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A רביעית of blood that comes out of a dead woman is impure both as a כתם and in an אהל.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: no כתם impurity, except on the birthing stool
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the blood is not impure as a כתם, because it came loose only after she died. He agrees that it is a כתם if she died while sitting on the birthing stool.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: it is not impure as a כתם, because it came loose after she died. But רבי יהודה agrees that if she was sitting on the birthing stool and died, and a רביעית of blood came out of her, it is impure as a כתם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the תנא קמא about the כתם impurity. He also gives one case where he agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, what matters is when the blood came loose. Blood that came loose after death is not a נדה's blood. A woman giving birth, though, already had blood coming loose while she was alive, so that blood is a כתם.

keyTerms.meaning: Came loose (literally, was uprooted) from its place in the body
The birthing stool a woman sits on during labor

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says:
it does not make things impure as a כתם,
because it came loose after she died.

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּיוֹשֶׁבֶת עַל מַשְׁבֵּר
phrases.english: And רבי יהודה agrees about a woman sitting on the birthing stool
who died, and a רביעית of blood came out of her,
that it makes things impure as a כתם.
phrases.notes: Here the blood had already started coming loose while she was still alive, during labor.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה מִשּׁוּם כֶּתֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's ruling about כתם impurity, and then gives an exception where he agrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood that came loose after death is not a כתם. Blood that came loose while she was alive, as on the birthing stool, is a כתם.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: so the birthing-stool blood is not impure in an אהל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says that, for that same reason, the blood in the birthing-stool case does not make things impure in an אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: Therefore, it does not make things impure in an אהל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי builds on רבי יהודה's birthing-stool case. He adds what this means for impurity in an אהל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood counts as a כתם because it came loose while she was alive, then it is a living woman's blood. It is not a dead person's blood, so it cannot carry the אהל impurity of a dead body.

phrases.english: רבי יוסי said:
Therefore, it does not make things impure in an אהל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: לְפִיכָךְ אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה בְּאֹהֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a further result from רבי יהודה's birthing-stool case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood in the birthing-stool case is not impure in an אהל, because it is a living woman's blood.

steps.title: Does the תנא קמא really call blood that came loose after death a כתם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes what seems to follow from the משנה: the תנא קמא holds that the blood is a כתם even though it came loose after she died. That seems hard to accept.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this imply that the תנא קמא holds that even though the blood came loose after she died, it still makes things impure as a כתם?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה with a question about the תנא קמא's view. This question sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה gave his reason as "because it came loose after she died." That suggests the תנא קמא disagrees even when the blood came loose after death. But a dead woman cannot become a נדה, so the גמרא finds this hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: Does this imply that the תנא קמא holds,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּנֶעֱקַר דָּם מִשֶּׁמֵּתָה,
phrases.english: that even though the blood came loose after she died,
it makes things impure as a כתם?
phrases.notes: The question is how blood from a woman who is already dead could have the impurity of a נדה's blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יהודה's reason to work out the תנא קמא's view, and questions it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied view of the תנא קמא that blood which came loose after death is a כתם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's reason implies the תנא קמא disagrees even when the blood came loose after death. But a dead woman cannot become a נדה, so that view seems hard to accept.

steps.title: The real dispute is whether the womb is an impure place
steps.stepSummary: רבי זעירי answers the difficulty from step 18. Everyone agrees that blood which came loose after death is not a כתם just by itself. The argument is whether the place of the מקור is impure, so that blood passing through it becomes impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זעירי said: The difference between them is whether the place of the מקור (the womb) is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 18. It explains what the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה really disagree about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 asked how the תנא קמא could call blood a כתם when it came loose only after death. רבי זעירי changes the reason. According to the תנא קמא, the womb is an impure place, so any blood that passes through it is impure even after death. רבי יהודה holds that passing through the womb does not make the blood impure.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'source', meaning the womb, where menstrual blood comes from
Its place is impure: the womb itself makes the blood that passes through it impure
There is a difference between them: the point the two opinions disagree about

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the תנא קמא holds that blood which came loose after death is a כתם on its own. רבי זעירי says the reason it is impure is that it passed through the womb.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ze'eiri said:
Whether the place of the source is impure
phrases.notes: The 'source' means the womb. The question is whether blood becomes impure just by passing through it.

phrases.english: is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי זעירי מקור מקומו טמא איכא בינייהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא seemed to hold that blood which came loose after death is a כתם just by itself
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא holds that the womb is an impure place, so blood that passes through it is impure. רבי יהודה disagrees.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה hold that the birthing-stool blood is impure in an אהל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'ומודה רבי יהודה'. It then asks about רבי יוסי's statement. If רבי יוסי says this blood is not impure in an אהל, does that mean רבי יהודה holds it is?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And רבי יהודה agrees.' Does this imply that the תנא קמא (here, רבי יהודה) holds that this blood also makes things impure in an אהל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the end of the משנה and makes an inference from רבי יוסי's words. That inference seems hard to accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says that, for that reason, the birthing-stool blood is not impure in an אהל. This suggests the opinion before him, רבי יהודה, holds that it is impure in an אהל. That seems strange, because this blood clearly left her while she was still alive.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication: we can infer from this
The first תנא, the opinion stated before the next one
A tent or roof. Impurity from the dead can spread to everything under the same roof.

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'תנא קמא' does not mean the first opinion of the משנה. It means רבי יהודה, because his statement comes right before רבי יוסי's.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda agrees.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה here: רבי יהודה agrees the blood is a כתם if she died on the birthing stool.

phrases.english: By implication, the first tanna holds
that it also makes things impure in a tent?

steps.triggerLanguage: מכלל דתנא קמא סבר באהל נמי מטמא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new part of the משנה, the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view of the birthing-stool blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's statement suggests that רבי יהודה holds the blood is impure in an אהל. But this blood came out while she was alive, so it should not carry the impurity of the dead.

steps.title: The dispute is about דם תבוסה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי disagree about דם תבוסה, which is blood that may have come out partly in life and partly after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The difference between them is דם תבוסה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 20. It gives the exact point that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי disagree about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that the blood of a woman who died on the birthing stool counts as דם תבוסה, a mix of blood from life and from death. So it is impure in an אהל by rabbinic law. רבי יוסי holds that this blood clearly came out while she was alive, so it is not דם תבוסה.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood that flows at the time of death, where it is unclear how much came out in life and how much after death

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Blood of submission is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יהודה דם תבוסה איכא בינייהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the specific point of dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seemed to hold that blood which left her in life is impure in an אהל like blood of the dead
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה treats this blood as דם תבוסה. רבי יוסי holds that it clearly came out in life and is not דם תבוסה.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines דם תבוסה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines דם תבוסה. It is blood from a killed person that flowed both while he was alive and after he died, when we are not sure how much came out at each stage.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: What is דם תבוסה? רבי אלעזר son of רבי יהודה explained: A killed person who lost blood both while alive and after death. Maybe it came out while he was alive, maybe after he died, maybe partly in life and partly in death. That is דם תבוסה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to explain the term דם תבוסה that רב יהודה just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דם תבוסה is a mix: we cannot tell which part of the blood came out before death and which part came out after. That doubt is what gives it its own special status. This explains why רבי יהודה can call the birthing-stool blood דם תבוסה, while רבי יוסי does not.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי זעירי: the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה disagree about whether the womb is an impure place. רב יהודה: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי disagree about whether the birthing-stool blood is דם תבוסה, the mixed blood of life and death.

phrases.english: As it is taught: What is blood of submission?
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yehuda explained:
A killed person from whom blood came out
both during his life and at his death,
maybe it came out during his life,
maybe it came out at his death,
maybe partly during his life and partly at his death:
that is blood of submission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term רב יהודה used in step 21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דם תבוסה is blood from a killed person that flowed both in life and in death, when it is unclear how much came out at each stage.

steps.title: The חכמים treat the doubtful blood as a regular doubt
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים respond to the ברייתא's first definition of דם תבוסה. They treat it as an ordinary ספק טומאה, which is impure in a רשות היחיד and pure in a רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: in a private area, when we are unsure, it is impure. In a public area, when we are unsure, it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the חכמים's reply to the first definition of דם תבוסה. They do not give it a special status. They treat it like any other doubt about impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case, we did not know whether the blood came out in life or after death. The חכמים say this is simply a doubt about טומאה. So we apply the usual rule: a doubt in a private area is impure, and a doubt in a public area is pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A private area. Here, a doubt about impurity is treated as impure.
A public area. Here, a doubt about impurity is treated as pure.
Its doubt: the case where we are not sure if it is impure.

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying this blood is always pure. The answer depends on where the doubt happened.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
in a private domain, its doubt is impure;
phrases.notes: The 'doubt' here is whether the blood came out in life or after death, as in the case just described.

phrases.english: in a public domain, its doubt is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד סְפֵקוֹ טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 22 with the חכמים's reply to the first definition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first case is a normal ספק טומאה: impure in a רשות היחיד and pure in a רשות הרבים.

steps.title: The חכמים's own definition of דם תבוסה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים define דם תבוסה as follows. A killed person lost a רביעית of blood both in life and after death. The blood is still flowing, and we do not know which part is larger, the part from life or the part from after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is דם תבוסה? A killed person lost a רביעית of blood while alive and after dying, and the blood has not yet stopped. It may be that most came out in life and a little after death. It may be that a little came out in life and most after death. That is דם תבוסה.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the first definition, the חכמים now say what the real דם תבוסה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here we know that blood came out both in life and after death, and it is still flowing. The doubt is only about the proportion between the two parts. The חכמים say that this mixed blood, with a mix we cannot measure, is what earns the name דם תבוסה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. This word replaces the earlier idea with a new one.
A quarter-לוג, the amount of blood from a dead person that makes things impure.
It has not stopped. The blood is still flowing.
Most of it / a small part of it.

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים: the first case is just an ordinary doubt. The real דם תבוסה is blood that came out both in life and after death, is still flowing, and has an unknown mix.

phrases.english: Rather, what is blood of submission?
A killed person from whom came out
a quarter-log of blood during his life and after his death,
and it still has not stopped,
it is uncertain whether most came out in his life and a little after his death,
or whether a little came out in his life and most after his death:
that is blood of submission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the first definition in step 23, the חכמים give their own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דם תבוסה is a רביעית of blood from a killed person that came out in life and after death, is still flowing, and has an unknown proportion between the two parts.

steps.title: Blood dripping into a hole: רבי יהודה against the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא continues: a killed person lies on a bed and his blood drips into a hole. רבי יהודה says the blood is impure because the 'drop of death' is mixed in. The חכמים say it is pure, and their reason continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: a killed person lost a רביעית of blood while lying on a bed, and his blood dripped into a hole. It is impure, because the drop of death is mixed into it. And the חכמים say it is pure, because...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 22 goes on to another case of blood from a killed person. רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about blood that collects in a hole. The amud ends in the middle of the חכמים's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that the blood in the hole is impure because it must include the drop that left the person at death. That drop is real 'death blood'. The חכמים disagree and call it pure. Their reason continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A hole or pit in the ground.
The 'drop of death': the drop of blood that leaves the body at the moment of death.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
a killed person from whom a quarter-log of blood came out,
and he was lying on a bed
and his blood was dripping into a hole:
it is impure,
phrases.notes: He means the blood that collected in the hole.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַטִּפָּה שֶׁל מִיתָה מְעוֹרֶבֶת בּוֹ.
phrases.english: because the drop of death is mixed into it.
And the Sages declare it pure, because

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הָרוּג שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ רְבִיעִית דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from steps 22–24 with another case of a killed person's blood, where רבי יהודה treats blood mixed with the drop of death as impure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: blood dripping into a hole from a killed person is impure because the drop of death is mixed in. The חכמים: it is pure (reason still to come).
